smell_validity.evidence: One responsibility (channel reachability) is spread across five sites in three files, each pinning verbatim header values locally, so rotating any channel value demands coordinated edits across check-in, polling, results, transport, and crypto. The verbatim-copy stealth makes the trap invisible on landing, a compelling case for why this fault deserves correction; the boundary from the single-header healthy design is unmistakable.

maintenance_impact.evidence: A lasting trap: every channel rotation requires hunting all pins, and missing one strands part of the beacon on stale infrastructure (the prompt's 2am scenario). Removing it restores the header as the one-place ownership boundary and stops repeated drift toward stale behavior and mistaken ownership, though for a small implant it is not an architecture-level shift.

development_plausibility.evidence: Models a sequence of individually defensible ops patches using natural C idioms (static arrays, a struct, an accessor), verbatim-copied realistic values, and believable 'hardening against header churn' comments that fit the repo's style. Comments are slightly over-expository about the smell's rationale, keeping it just short of indistinguishable-from-evolution authenticity.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: A strong engineering contract: bounds the task to a network-invisible cleanup toward a one-place edit, preserves wire bytes/cookie/encryption interop, keeps build/tests green, and excludes vendored crypto. 'Hunt everything, find one more' decisively prevents incomplete cleanup; the wire-identical constraint prevents wrong redesign. Materially reduces costly wrong direction and irrelevant redesign, a model description.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Five purposes (check-in, polling, results, transport, crypto) with at least two needing different decisions: transport requires reverting a template string plus heap-buffer exception cleanup; crypto requires reconciling the decrypt side with the unchanged encrypt side. Check-in stays a plain value swap, so not every counted purpose needs a distinct code-supported decision.

localization_burden.evidence: Requires combining across components (http.c fallback safety depends on main.c callers; crypto decrypt vs encrypt) and following aliases (the tasking_channel_host accessor, the beacon_endpoint struct). Plausible-looking locations must be excluded: encrypt_buffer's correct AES_KEY header use and doTasking. No second indirect mechanism, so not 5.

repair_coordination.evidence: Multiple shared rules span locations: cookie name across connectTrevor's parser and http_request's renderer; channel host across callers and the transport fallback; secret across encrypt and decrypt. Partial reversion leaves latent divergence on rotation. The cross-location rules are independent single shared rules, not two rules that demonstrably affect each other.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform rule, replace each pinned literal with its matching header macro, covers the value duplications (host x4, port x3, cookie x2, path, query key, secret), roughly two-thirds of locations. The http_request structural revert (template string, heap buffer and its free, host-fallback ternary) and the dead accessor/struct definitions need separate non-uniform handling.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Because every pin is a verbatim copy, an incomplete repair leaving a pin yields byte-identical wire traffic and passes the repo's limited tests silently. A partial http template/buffer revert produces a malformed Cookie header no wire-level assertion checks. Two distinct hidden failure paths, at least one unchecked by behavior; no today-failing multi-stage combination, so not 5.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
